meta.title: Bungalow 1 — Vayana Bungalows
meta.description: A private hardwood bungalow with garden views, plunge pool, and butler service. From $960 per night.

hero.title: Bungalow 1
hero.sub: A hardwood villa wrapped in trade winds, with an uninterrupted line to the horizon.

description.title: A hardwood retreat, open to the Black Sea.
description.p1: Set on a low rise above the lagoon, Bungalow 1 is a single-level pavilion of local hardwoods, with a deep timber deck, a salt-water plunge pool, and louvered walls that fold back to the trade winds.
description.p2: Inside, a king bed faces the sea through a wall of glass; a freestanding stone tub looks the same direction. Mornings begin with the sun coming up through the palms; evenings end with the lagoon's soft phosphorescence under the stars.
description.p3: Bungalow 1 includes a dedicated butler, twice-daily housekeeping, and a private outrigger berth at the resort dock for guests who'd like to take to the water on their own schedule.

meta.title: Bungalow 2 — Vayana Bungalows
meta.description: A two-level hilltop residence with infinity pool, private chef's table, and panoramic views. From $1,240 per night.

hero.title: Bungalow 2
hero.sub: A two-level hardwood pavilion above the lagoon, with the whole island laid out below.

description.title: A two-level pavilion above the lagoon.
description.p1: Bungalow 2 is a two-level hardwood pavilion set into the slope above the lagoon. The lower floor opens to a long infinity pool that reads, from the water, as a single sheet to the horizon; the upper floor is the private bedroom, with the island falling away in every direction.
description.p2: A chef's table on the deck seats six and is paired with a kitchen for in-residence dining; on most evenings the resort's executive chef will cook for guests on request, with a single-day notice. The view shifts every half hour from the trade-wind palms to the open sea.
description.p3: Bungalow 2 includes a dedicated butler, twice-daily housekeeping, and an electric buggy for the run down to the beach club. Children are welcome; the second bedroom converts to twin beds on request.

meta.title: Bungalow 3 — Vayana Bungalows
meta.description: A beachfront suite that opens directly onto the sand, with a private outdoor shower and a beach cabana. From $1,480 per night.

hero.title: Bungalow 3
hero.sub: Sand at your doorstep, the lagoon a few barefoot steps beyond.

description.title: Right on the sand, just above the tide.
description.p1: Bungalow 3 sits on the long shallow arc of the resort's main beach. The deck is the sand; a few steps from the bed and you're in the lagoon, where the water is calf-deep and warm for fifty metres out.
description.p2: Inside, the suite is a single open volume with a king bed, a deep tub on the seaward wall, and a soft palette of bleached oak and natural linen. A separate outdoor shower under the palms is the way most guests start the day.
description.p3: Bungalow 3 includes a dedicated butler, twice-daily housekeeping, and a private cabana on the beach with a daybed for two and a service bell. The cabana is the kind of place that quietly redraws an afternoon.

hero.title: On the Black Sea coast
hero.sub: A small port town on Bulgaria's southern Black Sea coast, framed by the Strandzha pine forest and a long ribbon of quiet beaches.

guide.lede: Tsarevo sits at the southern end of the Bulgarian Black Sea coast, where the Strandzha National Park's pine ridges run all the way down to the water.
guide.intro_para1: It's an old fishing port that grew slowly — small harbour, a single ridge, a tight grid of low-rise streets — and the seasonality is gentle. The beaches stretch in both directions: Veleka and Sinemorets to the south, the sweep of Tsarevo bay to the north, and a string of unnamed coves in between.
guide.intro_para2: It's reachable by car in a little over an hour from Burgas Airport (BOJ, ~85 km) and by a long drive from Sofia (SOF, ~410 km). Most guests fly into BOJ; the route hugs the coast from Burgas south, with the sea on the left almost all the way down.

beach.img_alt: A wide stretch of soft sand running into the Black Sea — characteristic of the long, quiet beaches around Tsarevo
beach.title: Beaches and coves
beach.body: Long open beaches give way to small, half-hidden coves the further south you walk. Veleka, just down the coast, is one of the cleanest river-mouth beaches in the country; the smaller bays north of town are reachable only on foot or by water and rarely crowded, even in August.

food.img_alt: An aerial view of clear turquoise water meeting a palm-fringed white sand beach
food.title: Restaurants and local food
food.body: Most of what's good is within walking distance of the harbour: fresh Black Sea catch, mussels and rapana from the bay, and a handful of small family kitchens that serve mezze under grapevines. A few inland wineries in the Strandzha foothills run tasting days through the warm months.

hiking.img_alt: A warm sunrise over a calm sea, with soft pink and gold light on the shoreline
hiking.title: Hiking and nature
hiking.body: Strandzha National Park — the largest protected area in Bulgaria — begins at the edge of town and runs inland for tens of kilometres. Marked trails follow the river valleys; the migratory bird routes overhead in spring and autumn are reason enough for a long walk, even if you don't normally count yourself a birder.

villages.img_alt: A jagged mountain peak rising above a sea of clouds at sunset, washed in pink and gold light
villages.title: Nearby villages and culture
villages.body: Sinemorets and Ahtopol are short drives down the coast, each with its own character — Sinemorets quieter and built around its river-mouth beach, Ahtopol with a working harbour and a small old town on a headland. Inland, Strandzha villages keep older traditions alive, including the fire-dancing rituals that the region is known for.
